_comment: Documented divergences of the JVM pattern-safety chain against the safety_gates corpus. Fail-closed: a failing case NOT listed here is red; a listed case that reproduces the reference verdict is red (stale baseline) EXCEPT for entries carrying the leading 'boundary' marker; a listed case whose observed divergent verdict no longer matches the recorded one is red (drifted entry). All entries are cost-verdict-mode TIMING facts: the corpus oracle is Python re + the reference synthesizer on the generating host, and the extrapolated cost of the synthesized probe sets is measured on THIS engine's executor (java.util.regex backtracking under the DeadlineCharSequence abort). The structural, compile, dangerous-construct and test-string probe layers reproduce every reference verdict (88/94 exact). Two entries are marked boundary: their extrapolated cost sits within a factor of ~1.5 of the 0.05s budget (0.053-0.073s vs 0.05), so ordinary host load-factor movement legitimately flips them between the divergent verdict and the reference verdict; for those, either outcome is accepted and any third verdict is red. The Go family documented the identical flip on safety_cost_verdict_safe_05 on its engine. Entry format: '[boundary ]safe=<bool>,reason_class=<class> :: <written reason>'.

cases.safety_gates/safety_cost_verdict_over_bu: safe=true,safe :: reference over-budget is a Python-re timing fact: (\d|\w)*; extrapolates past the 0.05s budget on the reference engine while java.util.regex executes the same probe sets far under the normalized budget (java's deterministic-loop optimization linearizes the single-char-body group), so the JVM arbiter accepts. The Rust family ledgered the identical case for the identical reason (its regex-crate NFA is also faster than Python re).
cases.safety_gates/safety_cost_verdict_structu: safe=true,safe :: reference rejects (a|aa)+$ because its probe timing on Python re crosses the budget and the nested-unbounded structural flag rides the over-budget reason; the JVM synthesizer reaches the pattern and java.util.regex times it under budget at the same cap, so the per-engine cost verdict accepts. Same root cause as the Rust family's ledger entry.
cases.safety_gates/safety_cost_verdict_safe_05: boundary safe=false,structural_unreachable_terminator :: opposite-direction timing fact at the budget boundary: on java.util.regex the greedy char-class backtrack over the prefix-flood probes measures 0.053-0.057s against the 0.05s budget at cap 10000 (a 6-14% over-margin), so an over-budget probe set returns the structural violation; Python re backtracks the same probes under budget and accepts. Host load-factor movement flips this verdict between the two outcomes, so either is accepted; a third verdict is red. The Go family logged this exact case flipping once under host load on its engine.
cases.safety_gates/safety_cost_verdict_safe_06: boundary safe=false,structural_unreachable_terminator :: java.util.regex measures the <script[^>]*> probe sets at extrapolated 0.057-0.073s vs the 0.05s budget (14-46% over, min 0.59-0.73s at 32000 chars, host-load normalized) where Python re measures under; the over-budget probe set returns the structural violation and the case rejects where the reference accepts. Boundary-class: either verdict is accepted, a third is red.
cases.safety_gates/safety_cost_verdict_safe_08: safe=false,structural_unreachable_terminator :: java.util.regex measures the \$\([^)]+\) probe sets at extrapolated ~0.19-0.26s, 4-5x the 0.05s budget, where Python re measures under; the rejection reason is the structural unreachable-terminator text riding the over-budget probe set.
cases.safety_gates/safety_cost_verdict_safe_09: safe=false,structural_unreachable_terminator :: java.util.regex measures the \$\{[^}]+\} probe sets at extrapolated ~0.249-0.260s, 5x the 0.05s budget, where Python re measures under; same divergence class as safety_cost_verdict_safe_08.
